newsitem.title: USA: US Sen Lugar to file futures-market bill - Aide.
newsitem.headline: US Sen Lugar to file futures-market bill - Aide.

text.p: Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar is expected to file soon a bill to update the Commodity Exchange Act, an aide said Thursday.

The bill would touch on a dozen areas, including a speed-up in the process of listing contracts for trading on exchanges and clarifying audit trail rules. It would not deal with hedge-to-arrive contracts, the aide said.
Lugar, Indiana Republican, indicated the bill was likely following a series of mid-year hearings on regulation of the futures industry.
The aide said a resolution was being sought between the Treasury and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on the so-called Treasury amendment, which involves financial instruments.
A draft report by the General Accounting Office said new variations on hedge-to-arrive contracts might be ruled by courts as illegal futures contracts, according to the Wall Street Journal.
The GAO said its report was not complete and would not be released until the fall.
There has been concern that sizable amounts of grain might be tied up in disputes over validity of the contracts.
